vectors.name: untrusted-default-off
vectors.description: Untrusted input cannot acquire include I/O merely by containing a directive.

vectors.name: dotdot-inside-root
vectors.description: Containment is decided after canonicalization, not by banning the dot-dot spelling.

vectors.name: dotdot-escape
vectors.description: A canonical target outside the configured root is denied.

vectors.name: symlink-file-escape
vectors.description: A file symlink inside the root cannot point to content outside it.

vectors.name: symlink-directory-escape
vectors.description: A symlinked directory component cannot escape the configured root.

vectors.name: absolute-escape
vectors.description: Opting into absolute paths still cannot escape the root.

vectors.name: missing-target-inside-root
vectors.description: A target whose canonical result is inside the root but does not exist is refused as missing, not as a containment denial: containment permits a path exactly when its canonical result stays inside the root.

vectors.name: missing-target-through-dotdot-inside-root
vectors.description: A missing target does not turn a permitted dot-dot spelling into an escape: the canonical result is inside the root, so the refusal is still a miss.

vectors.name: out-of-root-present-target-is-outside-root
vectors.description: The present half of the pair. A target whose canonical result is outside the root is a containment denial.

vectors.name: out-of-root-absent-target-is-outside-root
vectors.description: The absent half of the pair, identical to it but for the target being missing. Containment is decided on the canonical candidate, which is constructible for a missing path, so the refusal MUST NOT depend on whether the target exists: a resolver that reads first answers not-found here and outside-root above, and that difference is an existence oracle for paths outside the root.

vectors.name: out-of-root-through-present-directory-is-outside-root
vectors.description: The present half of the pair. The escape is routed through an intermediate directory that IS on disk, so the whole path canonicalizes in one step and the containment answer never depends on how a remainder is re-appended.

vectors.name: out-of-root-through-absent-directory-is-outside-root
vectors.description: The absent half, identical to it but for the intermediate directory being missing. The whole path no longer canonicalizes - POSIX resolution stops at the absent segment - so containment falls to the canonical candidate, and its remainder must have its dot-dot segments COLLAPSED before the answer is read off. Re-appending the remainder verbatim leaves a string that is lexically inside the root and fails the existence check instead, which reports the escape as not-found: no leak, but the refusal class now moves with whether an intermediate directory happens to exist.

vectors.name: remote-without-allowlist
vectors.description: A remote URL cannot trigger a fetch without an explicit host allowlist.

vectors.name: allowlist-does-not-require-fetching
vectors.description: An allowlist removes the prohibition but does not require remote support.

vectors.name: depth-stops-before-resolve
vectors.description: The first target beyond the depth limit is not passed to the resolver.

vectors.name: transitive-byte-budget
vectors.description: The byte budget is charged across the transitive graph.

vectors.name: repeated-target-charged-per-occurrence
vectors.description: Repeated includes are charged per occurrence, not per distinct identity.

vectors.name: budget-exhaustion-skips-later-resolver
vectors.description: After exhaustion, later siblings are refused without resolver I/O.

vectors.name: call-bound-on-unresolvable-targets
vectors.description: The call bound holds where the byte budget cannot reach: an unresolved target charges no bytes, so only a bound on invocations stops the I/O.

vectors.name: call-bound-exhaustion-skips-later-resolver
vectors.description: The directive AT the bound is resolved and charged; the one past it is refused without resolver I/O.

vectors.name: blank-root-spec-configures-no-root
vectors.description: A blank configured value is not a root. Section 19 requires a host to supply the root explicitly, and forbids the root defaulting to the process working directory - which is exactly where a blank spec lands when it is canonicalized instead of refused. Inclusion stays disabled, so a target that is inside the INTENDED root and exists is still not resolved.

vectors.name: relative-root-spec-configures-no-root
vectors.description: A root spec that is not absolute is not a root. A relative spec has no base the specification names, and every canonicalizer resolves one against the process working directory - the value section 19 forbids the root defaulting to, reached by a route the default rule does not cover. Inclusion stays disabled, so a target that is inside the INTENDED root and exists is still not resolved. This is the vector a trim-and-compare spelling cannot pass: "." is not blank after trimming, and only an absoluteness test refuses it.

vectors.name: whitespace-root-spec-configures-no-root
vectors.description: Whitespace-only falls out of the same rule rather than needing one of its own: "   " is a legal POSIX directory name, so it is refused because it is RELATIVE, not because it is blank. A directory genuinely named with spaces stays reachable by its absolute path.

vectors.name: absolute-root-spec-is-honored
vectors.description: An absolute configured value IS a root, and one wider than the including file's directory at that: the dot-dot target resolves. Without this a processor could refuse every spec and pin nothing.

vectors.name: absolute-root-spec-still-contains
vectors.description: The root a spec configures is the one it named, not a wider one: containment is still decided against it. Without this a processor could materialize every spec to the filesystem root and pass the vector above.
